newsitem.title: USA: Jury hits snag in Food Lion case.
newsitem.headline: Jury hits snag in Food Lion case.

text.p: A jury considering punitive damages against Walt Disney Co's ABC television network for a hidden camera report alleging that grocer Food Lion Inc sold spoiled products hit a snag Wednesday.

The jury sent a note to U.S. District Judge Carlton Tilley saying that one juror seemed to have decided in advance about the case and refused to negotiate. The panel asked the judge what to do to break the deadlock.
"We have one juror who refuses to negotiate on proposed figures 11 others are willing to consider. It has become very troublesome," the note said.

"This juror has taken a personal side to this trial, not based on evidence and documentation and instructions," the note said. "This juror seems to have their mind made up prior to negotiations and unwilling to work with the other jurors."

Tilley did not immediately indicate what he would do about the deadlock but invited lawyers from both sides to review an Allen charge, which advises jurors to listen to others and if persuaded, then negotiate a resolution.
The jury deliberated for five and a half hours Tuesday, the first day of deliberations, and resumed discussions at 0930 EST/1430 GMT Wednesday.
The hidden-camera report charged that Salisbury, North Carolina-based Food Lion sold spoiled meat and fish and used unsanitary food handling practices.
The program aired on PrimeTime Live in 1992.

Food Lion urged the jury to order ABC to pay "very large" damages for the report -- so large that the network, and others, would be deterred from conducting future hidden-camera reports that break the law in the process.

The jury hearing the case found late last year that ABC committed fraud, trespass and breach of loyalty when two producers worked undercover at Food Lion to film for the program and awarded Food Lion $1,400 in compensatory damages.
Food Lion is an affiliate of Belgium's Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION".
